content.value_statement: Inconsistent code patterns slow reviews and make refactors risky. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code clear standards for TypeScript, React, APIs, testing, and maintainability.
actual_capabilities: Defines readability, simplicity, DRY, and YAGNI principles for everyday development.
Gives TypeScript and JavaScript examples for naming, immutability, error handling, async work, and type safety.
Provides React guidance for typed components, hooks, state updates, and conditional rendering.
Documents REST API conventions, response formats, validation patterns, and error responses.
Covers project organization, comments, JSDoc, performance, testing, and code smell detection.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not run linters, tests, or formatters.
Examples focus on TypeScript, JavaScript, React, and Node.js projects.
Teams must adapt the standards to their architecture and domain rules.
The snippets are illustrative and are not complete production modules.

use_cases.title: Standardize a New Codebase
use_cases.description: Use the skill to set shared naming, structure, API, testing, and documentation expectations before development starts.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests Consistently
use_cases.description: Ask for a review against the standards to spot mutation, weak typing, unclear tests, and avoidable complexity.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Frontend Code
use_cases.description: Use the React and TypeScript examples to guide safer component, hook, state, and conditional rendering improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic Code Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check before opening a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript or JavaScript file against the coding standards. Focus on naming, readability, simple structure, and direct mutation.

prompt_templates.title: Improve React Components
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for a component or small feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the React standards to this component. Identify type gaps, state update risks, hook issues, and conditional rendering problems.

prompt_templates.title: Audit API Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for API routes and server handlers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these API route handlers against the standards. Check route naming, response shape, validation, error handling, and data selection.

prompt_templates.title: Create Team Review Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup for repeated repository reviews.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this repository context into a concise code review checklist based on the skill. Include TypeScript, React, API, testing, documentation, and performance checks.

output_examples.input: Review a pull request for TypeScript quality.
output: Flags unclear names, direct mutation, weak typing, and missing error handling.
Recommends immutable updates, descriptive names, and stronger function signatures.
Highlights missing validation, inconsistent response shape, and excessive selected fields.
Recommends a stable success and error envelope with narrow data selection.

output_examples.input: Improve test quality for a feature branch.
output: Suggests descriptive test names, Arrange-Act-Assert structure, and clearer edge case coverage.
Calls out vague tests that do not explain expected behavior.

best_practices: Use the skill before implementation to align on standards early.
Pair the skill with project linters, formatters, and tests for enforcement.
Ask for findings grouped by severity so review comments stay actionable.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the examples as complete application templates.
Do not apply every rule without considering project constraints.
Do not use the skill as a substitute for security review.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. It provides standards and review guidance through Markdown examples.

faq.question: Which languages does it focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Node.js, REST APIs, and related testing practices.

faq.question: Can it replace ESLint or Prettier?
faq.answer: No. Use it to guide decisions, then enforce formatting and rules with project tooling.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it for reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can apply the standards when reviewing or generating code.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: It includes validation and error handling guidance, but it is not a full security audit framework.

faq.question: Is it project-specific?
faq.answer: No. It gives general standards that teams should adapt to their architecture and domain.
